articles.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22.5% to ₹4,993 cr as fuel price freeze hits earnings
articles.description: State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs. BPCL's standalone net profit declined to Rs 4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from Rs 6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore from Rs 10,968 crore. India's second largest fuel retailer earned USD 32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to USD 10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back. But these gains were wiped away by losses arising from the five month old freeze in retail price revision despite a rise in cost. BPCL also booked Rs 330 crore ...
